ko_meaning_en: Things you wear on your body

example.en: I bought clothes at the market.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'clothes' the object.
form.why: 옷 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을. 를 follows a vowel, 이 marks a subject and 에 a place.

ko_meaning_en: Something you put on your feet to walk

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
에 marks the place where something is

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'shoes' the subject.
form.why: 신발 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이. 가 follows a vowel, and 을 marks an object.

ko_meaning_en: Something you wear on your head

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel
쓰다 also means 'to put on' a hat; -(으)세요 = polite request

form.q_en: Pick the verb Koreans use for putting on a hat.
form.why: Korean uses 쓰다 for hats and glasses and 입다 for clothes. 먹다 and 마시다 are for food and drinks.

ko_meaning_en: Something you put things in and carry around

example.en: There is a book in the bag.

tokens.note: 에 marks the place where something is

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the book is.
form.why: Use 에 for the place where something is (with 있다). 에서 is for where an action happens, and 을/를 mark objects.

ko_meaning_en: Clothes you wear on your legs

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: It happened yesterday. Pick the right verb form.
form.why: 어제 'yesterday' needs the past tense: 입 + 었어요 = 입었어요.

ko_meaning: 집에서 많이 키우고 '멍멍' 하고 짖는 동물
ko_meaning_en: An animal often kept at home that barks 'woof woof'

example.en: I saw a dog in the park.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
를 marks the object after a vowel
past tense, polite: 보 + 았어요 → 봤어요

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'dog' the object.
form.why: 개 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를. 을 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A small animal that says 'meow'

example.en: The cat sleeps on the bed.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'cat' the subject.
form.why: 고양이 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 이 follows a consonant, and 를 marks an object.

ko_meaning_en: An animal with wings that flies in the sky

example.en: There is a bird in the tree.

tokens.note: 에 marks the place where something is
가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: 'There are two birds in the tree.' Pick the number that goes before the counter 마리.
form.why: Animal counter 마리 uses native numbers, and 둘 becomes 두 before a counter. 이 and 삼 are Sino-Korean.

ko_meaning_en: A big animal that gives milk

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
present tense, polite: 주 + 어요 → 줘요

form.q_en: Pick the correct present polite form of 주다 'to give'.
form.why: 주 + 어요 contracts to 줘요. The other forms do not exist.

ko_meaning_en: An animal with a big nose that says 'oink oink'

tokens.note: 저 = polite 'I'; 는 marks the topic
안 before a verb makes it negative

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'pork' the object.
form.why: 돼지고기 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를. 을 follows a consonant, and 가 marks a subject.

ko_meaning: 모르는 사람을 물을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to ask about a person you don't know

form.q_en: Ask 'Who came?' Pick the right form of 누구.
form.why: Before the subject particle 가, 누구 shortens to 누가. 오다 needs a subject, not an object (를).

ko_meaning: 모르는 물건이나 일을 물을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to ask about a thing you don't know

example.en: What did you eat in the morning?

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Ask 'What did you eat?' (무엇 is the object).
form.why: 무엇 is the thing eaten, so it takes the object particle 을. 이 would make 'what' the eater.

ko_meaning: 모르는 곳을 물을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to ask about a place you don't know

tokens.note: 에서 marks the place of an action

form.q_en: Ask 'Where are you going this weekend?'
form.why: With 가다 the place you go to takes 에. 에서 is for where an action happens.

ko_meaning: 모르는 때를 물을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to ask about a time you don't know

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'is' after 언제.
form.why: 언제 ends in a vowel, so use 예요. 이에요 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A word used to ask for a reason

tokens.note: 안 before a verb makes it negative
past tense, polite: 오 + 았어요 → 왔어요

form.q_en: Say 'Why didn't you come yesterday?'
form.why: 안 goes right before the verb, and the past of 오다 is 왔어요.

ko_meaning_en: A word used to ask about the way to do something

example.en: How do you go to school?

form.q_en: Ask 'How do you go to school?'
form.why: 어떻게 asks about the way (how). 얼마 asks about price and 몇 about number.

ko_meaning: 값이나 양을 물을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word used to ask about a price or amount

form.q_en: Ask 'How much is the bag?'
form.why: 얼마 asks about price. 몇 must come before a counter, and 누구/언제 ask 'who'/'when'.

ko_meaning_en: A word used to ask about a number

example.en: How many people are in your family?

form.q_en: Ask 'How many apples are there?'
form.why: 몇 goes right before a counter (개, 명) to ask 'how many'. 얼마 asks about price.

ko_meaning_en: A thing close to the speaker

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: The thing is in your own hand. Ask 'What is this?'
form.why: 이것 is for things near the speaker. 그것 is near the listener, 저것 is far from both, and 여기 is a place.

ko_meaning_en: A thing close to the listener

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 그것.
form.why: 그것 ends in a consonant, so the topic particle is 은, not 는. 을 marks an object.

ko_meaning_en: A place higher than something

example.en: There is a computer on the desk.

tokens.note: 에 marks the place where something is

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the computer is.
form.why: With 있다 the place where something is takes 에. 에서 is for actions.

ko_meaning_en: A place lower than something

example.en: I read a book under the tree.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle: reading is an action.
form.why: Reading is an action, so the place takes 에서. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: The opposite of the back; the side your face looks toward

example.en: I meet my friend in front of the school.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: 'Please wait in front of the bank.' Pick the particle.
form.why: Waiting is an action, so the place takes 에서. 을 and 이 would make 앞 an object or a subject.

ko_meaning_en: The opposite side of the front

example.en: There is a mountain behind the house.

tokens.note: 에 marks the place where something is

form.q_en: 'The mountain is behind the house.' Pick the right form.
form.why: With 있다 the place takes 에: 뒤에. 에서 is for actions, and 를/가 do not fit here.

ko_meaning: 어떤 것의 오른쪽이나 왼쪽 가까운 곳
ko_meaning_en: The place just to the right or left of something

example.en: I sat next to my friend.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you sit.
form.why: 앉다 takes the place you sit with 에: 옆에 앉으세요 'please sit next to (my) friend'.

ko_meaning_en: The inner part of something

example.en: The child plays inside the room.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Ask 'What is inside the bag?' Pick the particle.
form.why: With 있다 the place where something is takes 에. 에서 is for actions.

ko_meaning_en: The place that is not inside

tokens.note: 비가 오다 = it rains; 오 + 아요 → 와요

form.q_en: 'I want to play outside.' Pick the particle.
form.why: Playing is an action, so the place takes 에서.

ko_meaning_en: The place where the speaker is

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel

form.q_en: Ask 'Where am I? (Where is here?)'
form.why: 여기 is the subject of 'where is it', so it takes 가: 여기가 어디예요?

ko_meaning_en: The place where the listener is

form.q_en: 'I'm going there now.' Pick the particle.
form.why: With 가다 the place you go to takes 에. 에서 is for where an action happens.

ko_meaning: 말하는 사람과 듣는 사람에게서 먼 곳
ko_meaning_en: A place far from both the speaker and the listener

example.en: The bus is coming over there.

form.q_en: You and your friend stand together and the bank is far away. Say 'The bank is over there.'
form.why: 저기 is far from both people. 여기 is near the speaker and 거기 near the listener.

ko_meaning_en: To feel good because something good happened

tokens.note: 저 = polite 'I'; 는 marks the topic

form.q_en: Pick the correct present polite form of 기쁘다.
form.why: 기쁘다 drops ㅡ before -어요: 기쁘 + 어요 → 기뻐요.

ko_meaning_en: To feel hurt inside because something bad happened

form.q_en: Pick the correct past polite form of 슬프다.
form.why: 슬프다 drops ㅡ in the past too: 슬프 + 었어요 → 슬펐어요.

ko_meaning_en: To feel glad and very good inside

form.q_en: Write a warm wish: 'Always be happy!'
form.why: 하다 words take -세요 directly: 행복하 + 세요 → 행복하세요.

ko_meaning: 싫은 일이 있어서 기분이 많이 나빠지다
ko_meaning_en: To feel really bad because something unpleasant happened

form.q_en: Pick the correct form: 'Why is Dad angry?'
form.why: 화나 + 았어요 contracts to 화났어요. Koreans use this past form to say someone is angry now.

ko_meaning_en: To feel worn out after doing a lot

example.en: I'm tired every day these days.

form.q_en: Say 'I'm not tired now.'
form.why: Put 안 right before a verb or adjective to say 'not'.

ko_meaning_en: To feel bad because your body is not well

form.q_en: Pick the correct present polite form of 아프다.
form.why: 아프다 drops ㅡ, and because the syllable before has ㅏ it takes -아요: 아파요.

ko_meaning: 목이 아프고 코에서 물이 나오는 병
ko_meaning_en: An illness where your throat hurts and your nose runs

example.en: My younger sibling caught a cold.

tokens.note: 감기에 걸리다 = to catch a cold
past tense, polite: 걸리 + 었어요 → 걸렸어요

form.q_en: Pick the particle: 'to catch a cold'.
form.why: Korean says 감기에 걸리다 (literally 'be caught by a cold'), so use 에, not 를.

ko_meaning_en: Something you take when you are sick

example.en: I took medicine in the morning.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the verb Koreans use for taking medicine.
form.why: In Korean you 'eat' medicine: 약을 먹다.

ko_meaning: 병원에서 아픈 사람을 낫게 해 주는 사람
ko_meaning_en: A person at a hospital who makes sick people better

example.en: My older sister is a doctor.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'is' after 의사.
form.why: 의사 ends in a vowel, so use 예요. 이에요 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 일을 하지 않고 몸을 편하게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To stop working and let your body relax

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: It happened yesterday. Pick the correct past form of 쉬다.
form.why: 쉬 + 었어요 = 쉬었어요 (ㅟ does not contract). 어제 needs the past, so 쉬어요 is wrong.

ko_meaning_en: A fully grown person

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle: 'Adults drink coffee.'
form.why: 어른 ends in a consonant, so the topic particle is 은, not 는. 을 marks an object.

ko_meaning_en: A person who works at a company

example.en: My dad is an office worker.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'is' after 회사원.
form.why: 회사원 ends in a consonant (ㄴ), so use 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The word used to call a person or thing

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
뭐 is the short spoken form of 무엇

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 이름.
form.why: 이름 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이. 가 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The number of years since you were born

form.q_en: Pick the word Koreans use to say someone is old.
form.why: Koreans say 나이가 많다 'to have many years' for being old.

ko_meaning: 두 사람이 한 가족이 되는 것
ko_meaning_en: Two people becoming one family

form.q_en: Say 'My older sister got married.'
form.why: 결혼 + 하다 = 결혼하다, and the past polite form of 하다 is 했어요.

ko_meaning_en: Telling about something in words

form.q_en: 'I talked with a friend.' Pick the particle for 이야기.
form.why: 이야기 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를: 이야기를 하다 'to talk'.

ko_meaning_en: Something you sing along with music

example.en: My younger sibling sings a song.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present polite form of 부르다 'to sing'.
form.why: 부르다 is 르 irregular: 부르 + 어요 → 불러요. 불어요 comes from 불다 'to blow'.

ko_meaning_en: Asking about something you don't know

form.q_en: 'The student asked a question.' Pick the particle.
form.why: 질문 ends in a consonant, so the object particle is 을: 질문을 하다 'to ask a question'.

ko_meaning_en: What you say back to a question

tokens.note: 안 before a verb makes it negative

form.q_en: Say 'The child doesn't answer.'
form.why: 안 goes right before 하다: 대답을 안 해요. 않 is used only in -지 않다.

ko_meaning_en: The language Korean people use

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the verb form that goes before 싶어요.
form.why: -고 싶어요 attaches to the verb stem: 배우 + 고 싶어요.
